admission.justification: The start ownership constrains every later leaf's seat preparation and is the base MIK-R100 builds on; the prohibited self-start shape is recorded, not claimed as a weighed design.

alternatives.option: The Manager starts the Worker and Reviewer together at leaf start and the Curator at the first freeze.
alternatives.reason: The starter briefs an agent and becomes its parent; keeping the three seats under one starter keeps the independent seats independent of the work they check.

alternatives.option: The Worker starts its Reviewer when a freeze exists and the Reviewer starts the Curator on code PASS.
alternatives.reason: The product refuses that start because the starter briefs and parents the agent it starts; the shape is recorded as prohibited, not as a seriously weighed design.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A later packet changes who may start a leaf's seats or admits a different starter for the set.

alternatives.option: The Orchestrator or Architect starts the leaf seats for a delegated master.
alternatives.reason: The leaf's checkpoint belongs to the Manager that owns the leaf's gate and transactions; higher seats keep their own starts.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A packet moves leaf-level starts to another named owner.

consequences: The Manager owns starts and replacements.
The Reviewer cold-reads first and the Curator starts exactly at the first freeze.
context: The three leaf seats need a starter, and a seat must not be able to start the one that checks it.
decider: the developer; D88, with the developer's direction of 2026-10-07 that the manager spawns them as a set
